segments.contextAfter: **Volatility**: This category lists *volatile* and *nonvolatile* resources. Nonvolatile memory total is a good indicator of your app’s tracked memory usage for Metal. When you mark a resource as volatile, you give Metal permission to dispose of its contents when memory is scarce. The operating system doesn’t count volatile memory in your app’s total memory footprint. For example, in iOS, a lower footprint reduces the risk that you exceed the jetsam limit and have the operating system terminate your app. If you think that you might use a resource in the future that you’re not currently using, mark it as volatile rather than simply releasing it. That way, you only need to recreate the resource’s contents if Metal discards them. For more information, see [`setPurgeableState(_:)`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Metal/MTLResource/setPurgeableState(_:)).
